newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end sharply mixed, nearbys off with cash.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end sharply mixed, nearbys off with cash.

text.p: CME hog futures closed sharply mixed with nearbys knocked lower by weakness in cash hog prices while summer month futures again advanced on Friday's bullish Hogs and Pigs Report, traders said.
Hogs finished 0.525 cent per lb lower to 1.300 higher with February off 0.525 at 78.700 cents. August paced the gain in summer months and set a new contract high of 73.400 cents.
Bear spreading and mixed selling pressure in nearbys reflected the sharp drop in pork cutout values and weak tone to cash hog markets. Cash hogs are also expected to be lower Friday, traders said.
"We should see another round of lower prices on Friday as the weather is good and the packer has been able to obtain the needs fairly easy," said Dave Maher, analyst for Securities Corp of Iowa.
Maher noted that packer margins are $4 in the red and the weakness in cash pork prices will keep bids for cash hogs down until cutout margins improve.

Deferred months were again buoyed by the USDA hog report which indicated fewer hogs than had been expected. Hog numbers will likely be under year-ago levels into at least the fall of 1997 before rising, traders said.

Rand Financials notably sold February and April early with E.D.&F. Man and Rosenthal Collins pressuring April, traders said. However, ran bought February late. Spreaders sold February and bought April and June, pit sources said.
In hog options, commission house bought 78 and 79 February puts and sold 78 to 82 calls following the break in futures. Volitility was easier in February, pit sources added.

Pork bellies pared losses late on local short covering but remained at net losses on pressure from expectations that higher cash belly prices would cut off user demand and spillover weakness from nearby hog futures, traders said.
Also, analysts earlier noted that Tuesday's weekly CME out-of-town belly report showed a larger than expected in-movement.
Pork bellies closed 0.875 to 0.675 cents a lb with Febraury off 0.850 at 81.500 cents.
